dependency.service: kafka ('orders' topic; checkout producer -> accounting consumer -> Postgres)

readback.locator: [2.75-A BOUND] SELECT street_address FROM accounting.shipping WHERE street_address='<the request-derived marker>' on the postgresql pod (db otel; schema accounting - a bare \dt shows only public and misleads). The accounting Postgres row is the SUT's ONLY durable record of a placed order (no user-facing order query API exists). KEY = the request-derived street_address marker, NOT the server-assigned order_id (which the oracle forbids as a correlation key); accounting persists Order+Shipping+OrderItem in ONE SaveChanges() transaction, so a street_address-keyed absence is equivalence-preserving vs the order_id-keyed capture locator (review C-R2). The Phase-D capture-of-record keyed on accounting."order".order_id; this bound locator is the 2.75-A enablement form.

config.note: kafka deployment scaled to 0 while POST /api/checkout executes. The swallow is UNMODIFIED SUT source: checkout's sendToPostProcessor publishes to the Kafka 'orders' topic asynchronously and only LOGS delivery failures - PlaceOrder acks 200 regardless (survey: src/checkout/main.go, 'Kafka publish swallowed'). With the broker down the message NEVER EXISTS anywhere durable, so the loss is PERMANENT (nothing to drain on restore) - unlike an accounting-down fault, where messages buffer in the topic and land late (pending vs missing). Restore = scale kafka back to 1 PLUS the measured recovery runbook: a REPLACED kafka pod (emptyDir storage, new cluster id) wedges BOTH rdkafka clients - the old checkout producer keeps silently losing acked orders PAST the restore and the old accounting consumer stops consuming - so checkout+accounting+fraud-detection are rollout-restarted after any kafka pod replacement.

fault.injected_by: runner (kubectl scale), out of band of the capture driver

stimulus.script: POST /api/cart (product 0PUK6V6EV0, session uuid) -> POST /api/checkout (kafka down) -> GET /api/cart observation; runner-level psql read-back

ground_truth.label: positive
ground_truth.rationale: The flagship ASYNC acked-but-lost, natural in the unmodified SUT: PlaceOrder returns a full 200 order confirmation (orderId, shipping tracking id, totals) while the Kafka publish that feeds the accounting ledger is swallowed - the vendor's own source only logs the delivery failure and acks anyway (src/checkout/main.go sendToPostProcessor). The accounting Postgres row is the system's only durable record of the order, and it never lands (measured: absent in-window, absent after broker restore, absent after a later canary proves the pipeline healed - the loss is permanent, not delayed). NORM (docs/source): the demo's own architecture docs describe accounting as the service that 'processes incoming orders' from the orders topic into its ledger; an order acked to the user that permanently never reaches the ledger violates that documented flow, and nothing in the 200 response communicates it.
ground_truth.doc_citation: open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo 2.2.0: src/checkout/main.go (sendToPostProcessor - Kafka publish errors logged, order acks regardless); docs service table (accounting consumes 'orders' topic and persists); survey row debug/a-main/c2c3/c2-depth-survey.md (OTel-Demo, 'Kafka publish swallowed').
